hints.title: Collect one common exponent
hints.body: Use b2x=(b2)x and c3x=(c3)x. Since the bases are positive, the product becomes (ab2c3)x.
hints.recap: Positive-base index laws combine factors with the same exponent.
hints.pitfall: The new base is a product, not <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pause: Write the equation using the single base <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Positive-base index laws combine factors with the same exponent.

hints.title: Take logarithms
hints.body: Take a logarithm in the same valid base on both sides of the single-base exponential equation. Apply the logarithm power rule to bring the unknown exponent down as a multiplier.
hints.recap: The logarithm power rule brings the unknown exponent down as a multiplier.
hints.pause: Write the logarithmic equation and rearrange it for the unknown exponent.

recall.reminder: The logarithm power rule brings the unknown exponent down as a multiplier.

hints.title: Check the divisor
hints.body: If ab2c3=1, the left side of the original equation would always be 1, never 2. The stated equation therefore ensures that its logarithm is nonzero.
hints.recap: Verify a denominator is nonzero before dividing.
hints.pitfall: Do not place the whole quotient inside one logarithm.
hints.pause: Derive an exact expression for the exponent, check the divisor and verify your expression in the logarithmic equation.

recall.reminder: Verify a denominator is nonzero before dividing.

solution:
Positive bases allow axb2xc3x=(ab2c3)x. Taking base-10 logarithms gives xlog10(ab2c3)=log102.

The combined base cannot equal 1 for an equation whose right-hand side is 2. Its logarithm is therefore nonzero, and division gives x=log102log10(ab2c3), option F.
knowledgePattern: Combine exponential factors before taking logarithms
